video_title: What Does ESPN's Latest Statement on the Clippers Mean? (ft. Pablo Torre)

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Don Van Natta Jr.'s status as a top ESPN investigative journalist
quotes.excerpt: Don Van Natta Jr. is by resume the single best journalist in the history of ESPN.

text_blocks.speaker: Dan Le Batard
text_blocks.text: When I make the argument that Don Van Natta Jr. is by resume the single best journalist in the history of ESPN, are there many rebuttals to that?

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: It just depends on how you measure awards. He has been a part of three Pulitzer Prize-winning teams. I know Don pretty well. I have reported the same stories at various points in our overlapping careers as Don. I did not see this coming, broadly speaking. There are many other great journalists who have worked for ESPN and elsewhere in sports media, but his resume in terms of the decoration of the awards and prizes is hard to beat.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Impact of the ESPN story on Steve Ballmer and the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: I have a theory that that story made everything here worse for Steve Ballmer and the Clippers.

text_blocks.speaker: Dan Le Batard
text_blocks.text: I have a theory that this ESPN story, while it ends up making that report come out, I have a theory that that story made everything here worse for Steve Ballmer and the Clippers. But Don Van Natta Jr. might be thinking that his sources were telling him what they thought was right at the time and he believed his sources. That this isn't a matter of ego and a journalist doubling down on ego, it's that he really thinks that his reporting at the time was right.

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: Based on what I have known, based on what I have reported, based on what has come out, based on what the Clippers posted from their official Twitter account within minutes, within the same hour that the ESPN story came out, this was from the Clippers. And the NBA thinks that, I think that the Clippers PR statement indicates that I have found no evidence that this is not exactly what was most beneficial to the Clippers. And in fact, according to my reporting, fed from the Clippers to ESPN.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The Walk-Tell Report and the Clippers' PR statement
quotes.excerpt: It led to the publishing of the Walk-Tell Report.

text_blocks.speaker: Dan Le Batard
text_blocks.text: What does this say about what changed here, Dan?

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: The first thing is that it led to the publishing of the Walk-Tell Report. I was told before this ESPN story came out, in no uncertain terms, do not expect the report after ESPN's story comes out and the NBA comes out and says significant and numerous inaccuracies. Suddenly now we have the 35 to 36 pages with the cover sheet report. The framing of the story, as well as the specific paragraphs in the story, it's not just a matter of we were right, but the framing was bad. It's there were many things like no evidence of funneling money through Clippers sponsors that by any reasonable measure was wrong. My reporting says that the Clippers fed ESPN a version of their legal defense and sold it as the facts that the NBA obtained.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers owners' reaction to the ESPN story
quotes.excerpt: They were fighting about whether Ballmer would even want to negotiate a settlement.

text_blocks.speaker: Dan Le Batard
text_blocks.text: How pissed off was the NBA about that ESPN story? Because I really do think, Pablo, and you need to correct me because you're the one who's doing the reporting, I really think that what happened is as soon as that report came out, throughout all of those owners with all of that money, it was a giant, 'Hey Ballmer, all right, fuck you, watch this.'

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: They were fighting. They were fighting about whether Ballmer would even want to negotiate a settlement. It was fighting about all of it. So yes, this is a rare thing. It's a rare thing that I said at the time for Mike Bass, the chief comms guy, to put his name on a statement that is that bold. It demands that you back up what you meant. And now we know. They don't release the Walk-Tell Report if ESPN's story does not come out.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The NBA's motivation for withholding the Walk-Tell Report
quotes.excerpt: One of the big reasons the NBA did not want to release that report is because they didn't want me to do more podcasts about it.

text_blocks.speaker: Dan Le Batard
text_blocks.text: What does that statement look like in your opinion if that ESPN story doesn't exist and you never see and we never see this 35, 36-page report?

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: All of it is premised on a negotiated settlement which would have brought the penalties lower. The NBA has no interest in doing this. One of the big reasons the NBA did not want to release that report is because they didn't want me to do more podcasts about it. We have been annoying. We have been a thorn in the side of people who want this story to be smaller. They have been aligned until that ESPN story in terms of the public view on, we would like these podcasts to stop and we would like this story to go away.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's history of not wanting to settle
quotes.excerpt: He doesn't want to settle and he has never, just characteristically, when he ran Microsoft and was the federal government in antitrust, he did not want to bend the knee.

text_blocks.speaker: Dan Le Batard
text_blocks.text: Doesn't this ultimately come down to, this is a man, Steve Ballmer, who always gets what he wants?

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: He doesn't want to settle and he has never, just characteristically, when he ran Microsoft and was the federal government in antitrust, he did not want to bend the knee. In this case, he is being asked elsewhere as a member of the NBA's audit committee, which is a perfect detail about the board of governors. He is on the audit committee, Steve Ballmer is. He is being asked to also fund NBA Europe and all these other projects I am sure that Adam Silver would like. He is somebody who is asked on various levels, can you help fund this?

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: Owners' fear of Steve Ballmer's spending habits
quotes.excerpt: What they're afraid of is they'll have to do what he did.

text_blocks.speaker: David Samson
text_blocks.text: It's not Steve Ballmer and the money that the other owners are afraid of. What they're afraid of is they'll have to do what he did. It's not about whether the report was ever released and Pablo and I may disagree about this. It's about, in order to compete, because this is how owners think and presidents think, I don't want to have to compete with someone who's willing to do what he did in order to get a player. And Pablo and I were at a show once and someone actually said to us something very similar from another team, which was, 'What worries me the most is I'm going to have to look my owner in the face and say, hey, if you want this player, you're going to have to circumvent the salary cap.' That's what the owners were trying to avoid, not fighting.

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: It was a bit more pointed. It was something along the lines of, if they don't get punished for this, I'm going to have to learn how to do money laundering.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's need to settle the civil lawsuit
quotes.excerpt: Steve Ballmer has to get Kawhi Leonard traded, Steve Ballmer has to figure out the civil suit.
quotes.quote: Steve Ballmer has to get Kawhi Leonard traded, Steve Ballmer has to figure out the civil suit because it doesn't matter whether he's exposed for 50 million or 100 million or 200 million. Where Ballmer has his point of concern is when it gets to be criminal, when it gets to be government intervention where there could be a situation that really does force a sale of the Clippers or force a loss of freedom. Whatever the case may be, it wouldn't be this, but it certainly could be the sale of the Clippers if he's found to have done things that we have not reported or don't know about quite yet. So at some point Dan, Ballmer will realize that being quiet is the only move he has.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The SEC's investigation into the Clippers and Steve Ballmer
quotes.excerpt: The SEC has asked us for information related to the Kawhi deal.
quotes.quote: The SEC has asked us for information related to the Kawhi deal. And then hours later we got what Walk-Tell knew about the Kawhi-Dectronics deal, in addition to what we had reported. And there's more. There are other companies they did this with which we are continuing to investigate. And so this is not just cap circumvention, although that might be the emotional lever on Steve Ballmer's ego, perhaps the paramount one. The other stuff is the real-world stuff that David was just alluding to, and his lawyers, there's a difference between rattling a saber and threatening litigation which you can do without penalty forever. There's a difference between that and what actually you got to show and prove when it comes to a civil proceeding that you want to dismiss, an SEC probe that you got to answer questions from, and a Kawhi trade you need processed because you can't do that unilaterally, you need others in the league to actually cooperate with you.
